But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.title: Stephen A. Smith visits White House again after controversial dinner with President Trump
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Last month, Stephen A. Smith met with United States President Donald Trump for what turned out to be a high-profile and controversial dinner. On Thursday, the ESPN star was back at the White House. Smith’s last visit, a dinner alongside Bill Maher and Kid Rock, drew plenty of backlash and ended with Trump publicly trashing the evening as a “waste of time.” But that did not seem to stop Smith from visiting again this week. Dinner With Trump Back in October, Trump had a high-profile dinner with Smith, Maher, and Kid Rock where the four discussed a number of topics for hours. Kid Rock was the first to share details about the dinner , saying the group discussed everything from the war in Iran to socialism. Smith said he went to advocate for HBCU funding. “Anytime I see HBCUs in trouble, I’m going to do what I can to help,” Smith said, via The Comeback . “It’s just that simple.” Smith said the dinner lasted more than four hours, and he compared Trump to legendary boxing promoter Don King. Trump, however, later disputed Smith’s account in a lengthy social media post. “I learned nothing, and felt it was a waste of time,” Trump wrote. “It didn’t last four hours, it lasted two hours, maybe less.” Trump also called Maher a “COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER” and a “major POTHEAD” in the same post. Back at the White House While Trump may have dismissed the meeting as a waste of time, that does not seem to have scared Smith away. On Thursday, CBS News shared video of Smith arriving at the White House. The network noted that Smith “was seen walking into the West Wing.” The White House has not said why Smith was there. Smith has not yet commented on the visit. Given how much Smith had to say about his last trip to the White House, though, he probably won’t stay quiet about this one for long. Stephen A.’s Political Ambitions Smith has repeatedly floated the idea of running for president in 2028 as a Democrat. But he hasn’t always made it easy to tell where he stands politically, often taking shots at both parties. He has called out Trump for making “utterly ridiculous” promises, and said Republicans had “no spine whatsoever” against the president. But he also recently praised Secretary of State Marco Rubio as “the real deal” and predicted he will be the Republican nominee in 2028. Smith added that he hasn’t seen a Democrat who can beat him yet. Smith’s political future may face an uphill battle regardless. A recent poll showed that neither side of the aisle is particularly fond of him. The post Stephen A. item.title: Klopp praises Kimmich, keeps starters for Serbia match under wraps
item.description: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp attends a press conference at Rajko Mitic Stadium, ahead of Friday's UEFA Nations League soccer match against Serbia. (is associated with: «Klopp praises Kimmich, keeps starters for Serbia match under wraps») Christian Charisius/dpa Jürgen Klopp, Germany's men's national football coach, already has his starting line-up in mind for the Nations League match against Serbia on Friday, but he's not talking. "If nothing happens overnight, I know how we will start," Klopp told reporters on Thursday ahead of the match, which starts at 8:45 pm (1945 GMT) at the Belgrade stadium. Klopp, 59, did not confirm the expected appearance of captain Joshua Kimmich. However, he lavished praise on the star player. "Jo Kimmich is a superplayer." Kimmich was not in the squad that beat Serbia 2-0 in the first leg in Munich. At that game, Kimmich's Bayern colleagues Aleksandar Pavlović and Tom Bischof put in top midfield performances alongside Florian Wirtz. Klopp called that game just a "blueprint" for him. The German coach had already committed to Marc-André ter Stegen as the number one goalkeeper when nominating the squad. He had also confirmed Bayern player Jonathan Tah in defence. Aim: a "final" against the Netherlands Klopp's immediate goal is to keep alive the German team's chances of reaching the Nations League quarter-finals with a second win against the winless Serbs. "We feel well prepared," Klopp said after four training sessions. He said everyone wants to earn "a final" for the last group game on Monday in Berlin against the Netherlands. Klopp said the fifth international match under his leadership was a test of how far the team has come. He regretted that only several thousand Serbian children will be admitted to the stadium because of a spectator ban.

item.title: Newark Catholic volleyball falls in Division VII state semifinal
item.description: Another championship season for the Newark Catholic volleyball team has come to an end. NC was unable to sustain a fast start Nov. 12 in a loss to Fort Loramie, 27-25, 25-18, 25-19, in a Division VII state semifinal at Wright State. The Green Wave (21-5) were reigning Division VI state champions and hoping stay on top but fell to Fort Loramie (23-4), the 2024 Division VII state champion. Leah Caudill recorded 15 kills in her final match for NC, which led 9-1 in the first set before Fort Loramie came charging back, eventually scoring six of the final seven points. The New York Jets ’ biggest mistake at the 2026 trade deadline was keeping Breece Hall . They had a rare chance to cash in at running back and instead protected a backfield that now works against its best young player, Braelon Allen. At 2-7, they were in a position to sell, and the one trade they made involved a backup safety. Quiet Deadline for a Losing Team The Jets’ only trade was sending safety Andre Cisco to Detroit for a 2028 sixth-round pick . Ian Rapoport reported edge rusher Will McDonald IV had asked to be traded, and Jets players on expiring deals drew interest. The Jets were only interested in moving expiring contracts, preferring to keep their 2027 roster intact. That approach is hard to defend for a team that is 5-21 in the Aaron Glenn era. A rebuilding club should be collecting assets, not protecting veterans who may not be part of the next good roster. The Jets did that last year when they traded Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams. This year, they stood pat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Why Hall Was the Right Trade Chip John Jones-Imagn Images Hall was the most obvious candidate. Allen filled in during Hall’s five-game absence with a quad injury, rushing for 504 yards and two touchdowns in five starts. He had three 100-yard games in that stretch, and that 504 yards is more than Hall has gained in any five-game stretch of his career. The financial case was just as strong. Allen is on his rookie contract at roughly $1.2 million this season and $1.3 million in 2027. Hall signed a three-year extension in May worth $43.5 million. The Jets would have taken only a $5 million dead-cap hit in 2026 and $4 million in 2027 while gaining around $10 million in space. Hall was also due to return at a moment when contenders needed running backs. Trading him would have turned a surplus into picks and given Allen a clean path. Kansas City reportedly offered a third-round pick for Hall a year earlier, which shows the market exists. Allen’s Role Now Looks Muddled The Jets said they would not trade Hall, and they did not. item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Robert Griffin III reveals stance on Nick Sirianni, Jalen Hurts’ Eagles futures appeared first on ClutchPoints . The moves come amid the Eagles’ current seven-game losing streak, with the team falling apart at the seams, primarily due to injuries. Now, former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III has taken to social media to reveal his take on the future of two key members of the Eagles. “The Eagles’ season is lost, but they shouldn’t fire Nick Sirianni or trade Jalen Hurts this offseason,” wrote Griffin III on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sirianni has long been one of the most polarizing coaches in the NFL today. On the one hand, Philadelphia consistently has churned out winning seasons (this year aside) under his watch, and have also won a Super Bowl and appeared in another. On the other hand, the Eagles have had some clear signs of friction with Siriannia at the helm, including the coach himself shouting at the home fans and suffering some puzzling playoff losses and late-season meltdowns. item.title: Ferrari’s F1 Team Is Worth $8.2 Billion, and Even Last-Place Cadillac Is Worth $2.7B
item.description: Ferrari is worth $8.2 billion, the most of any F1 team for the fourth year in a row, and even Cadillac, the grid’s least valuable team, is worth $2.7 billion in its first season, according to Sportico ’s new team valuations. The average F1 team is now worth $4.55 billion. That’s up 33% on last year, or 39% if you leave out Cadillac, which joined in 2026 and pulls the average down. It follows a 48% rise last year, and the average has almost tripled since 2023. Sportico says no other major league comes close over that stretch. The next best are the NHL, up 85% since 2023, and the NFL, up 81%. Ferrari Tops the List for a Fourth Straight Year Liam Lawson leads Lando Norris and the field at the start of the F1 São Paulo GP. Image Credit: Manuel Eletto/Sutton Images via Getty Images/Red Bull Content Pool Ferrari’s value is up 28% on last year. Mercedes is second at $7.75 billion (up 32%), McLaren is third at $6.3 billion (up 33%) and Red Bull is fourth at $5.6 billion (up 30%). Aston Martin is fifth at $4.15 billion, up 38%, even though it’s 10th in the constructors’ standings. New York Jets owner Woody Johnson bought more than 15% of the team this summer at a value of about $4.7 billion, Sportico reported. Alpine is sixth at $3.28 billion (up 58%), and Williams is seventh at $3.24 billion (up 51%). Cadillac Is Worth $2.7 Billion in Its First Season Racing Bulls, on course for fifth in the constructors’ championship, is eighth at $3.05 billion (up 49%). Red Bull turned down a billion-dollar bid for the team. Audi is ninth at $3 billion (up 60%), and Haas, the other American-owned team, is 10th at $2.8 billion (up 67%). Cadillac is last at $2.7 billion, with no figure from last year because it only joined the grid in 2026. Its owners, TWG Global and General Motors, paid a $450 million fee to enter and put in at least another $1 billion to get the team running. TWG boss Mark Walter is now shopping his stake with an asking price of at least $3 billion. Together, the 11 teams are worth $50 billion. These are Sportico ‘s estimates rather than sale prices, built from its own sums and from interviews with team owners, executives, bankers, lawyers and investors. item.title: After World Cup experience, Leo Nannetti shares lessons with Brazil U20s
item.description: After World Cup experience, Leo Nannetti shares lessons with Brazil U20s Brazil’s youth national teams are the natural pathway to the senior side. Goalkeeper Leo Nannetti, however, landed a golden ticket and got a “sneak peek” at life with the Seleção during the 2026 World Cup, when he was invited to join the squad and had the privilege of training alongside his idols. Now he is putting that experience to work with the U-20s and sharing what he learned with his teammates. Nannetti’s first opportunity with Brazil came with the U-17 national team in 2024, when he played in the Cascais Luso Cup. In 2025, however, he skipped a step: he joined the senior squad for training at Granja Comary ahead of World Cup qualifiers against Chile and Bolivia. In 2026, the invitation was like a VIP pass: he attended the World Cup and trained alongside Alisson, Ederson and Weverton under Taffarel’s guidance, experiencing the tournament atmosphere firsthand. Leo Nannetti: U-17 call-ups and invitations to train with the senior national team already on his résumé, and now looking forward to a tournament with the U-20s Credits: Joilson Marconne / CBF “I never imagined I would be experiencing a World Cup atmosphere at 18. It added so much to my career and my personal life. I was alongside my idols, watching how they conduct themselves, how they train and how they prepare for each game. I’ll carry that experience with me for the rest of my life,” he said. Naturally, these experiences spark curiosity among his teammates, although most already play for their clubs’ senior teams. Nannetti shares what he can and draws on the experience he has gained throughout his career to keep improving with Brazil’s U-20s. The goalkeeper has been working hard in training in Belém ahead of two friendlies against Peru Credits: Joilson Marconne / CBF “A lot of them ask what it was like, and I always try to answer as naturally as possible. The technical and mental demands change a lot from one national team to the next. The U-17s are more about development, the U-20s are very competitive, and the senior team—well, that goes without saying, doesn’t it? The pressure they carry, representing an entire nation,” he said. The goalkeeper considers one thing essential: keeping each of these experiences in perspective so he can continue developing. “I always try to keep my feet on the ground. If I’m here today, I have God, coach Paulo Victor and the coaching staff to thank for believing in my work. And I have to remember that being called up now doesn’t mean I’ll be at the South American Championship. It’s an important step, but I give my best in every training session to try to secure my place in the squad,” he concluded. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: ‘I Still Talk to Him’: Aaron Rodgers Looks Forward to Reuniting with Mike Tomlin on Sunday Night
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike Tomlin after the Steelers' 34-32 win over the New York Jets on Sept. 7, 2025. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has tuned in to watch Mike Tomlin on NBC’s Football Night in America this season. He thinks his former head coach is a natural as an analyst. “I’m not surprised in the least,” Rodgers said of Tomlin turning heads in his new role. “He is absolutely killing it on TV the few times I’ve seen him. Nobody can talk football better than Mike T, so it is an absolute match made in heaven. Him being on TV and doing what he does. And I don’t know if he still wants to coach at some point, but he’s doing a hell of a job.” Tomlin will see his former team up close and in person for the first time on Sunday night since resigning in January. “I look forward to it because of the relationships, but you know me, I’m capable of compartmentalizing, and getting hyper-focused on the job,” Tomlin said on a conference call with NBC Sports on Wednesday. “But it certainly will be fun to see some guys I got relationships with and there’ll certainly be a lot of those. But they have a job to do, I have a job to do, and so I’m sure everyone’s going to be focused on the task at hand.” Rodgers still keeps in touch with Tomlin. “I still talk to him,” Rodgers said. “I love Mike T, and I have so much appreciation for him bringing me here last year and the amount of fun that we had together. The closeness of the bond that we formed. So it’ll be good to see him.” “I’m having a lot of fun,” Tomlin said. “Haven’t given one iota of thought about coaching. The Browns are 3-0 at home this year, but after having lost two straight games, they are being treated like an afterthought this week. As you can see in the national picks below, not a single person is picking the Browns at home. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 10 game between the Browns and Texans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Texans: Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley’s unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers’ league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who’s allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud’s other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston’s lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns’ permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans’ team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that’s going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he’ll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That’s a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. item.title: Braves Sign Evan Phillips To $35 Million Deal Eight Years After Trading Him Away
item.description: Atlanta Braves pitcher Evan Phillips The Atlanta Braves have made the first big splash in free agency by signing former Los Angeles Dodgers reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal. The Braves announced in a press release that Phillips will make $11 million in 2027 and 2028, and $13 million in 2029. He will also donate 1% of his salary to the Atlanta Braves Foundation. The Braves originally drafted Phillips in the 2015 MLB Draft, and he made his MLB debut with them in 2018. He was traded to the Baltimore Orioles that same year in a deal that landed the Braves Kevin Gausman and Darren O'Day. Since then, he has also played for the Tampa Bay Rays and the Los Angeles Dodgers. He has been with the Dodgers since 2021 and has been key in their success. Since joining the Dodgers, he has posted a 2.36 ERA in 232 games. From 2022-2024, he pitched in 187 games with a 2.21 ERA and notched 44 saves. In 2025, he underwent Tommy John surgery and did not return until July of last season. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Last season, he ended up pitching in 31 regular-season games with a 3.46 ERA. He also threw three scoreless innings in the postseason. Phillips is 32 years old and still has some good baseball left in him. The Braves won't need him to close games, as they already have Robert Suárez, who is very capable of closing games if Raisel Iglesias leaves in free agency. If Iglesias does return, the Braves will have an even better bullpen than last season, with Phillips now in the mix as well. Phillips won the World Series with the Dodgers in 2024, throwing 6 2/3 scoreless innings in the postseason. He was injured for the World Series run in 2025, however. item.title: Sophie Cunningham names the LA Lakers player she should be compared to instead of Luka Doncic
item.description: Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images WNBA star Sophie Cunningham instantly distanced herself from a statistical comparison to Luka Doncic, and pointed the conversation in another direction. Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham discussed the Los Angeles Lakers on the latest episode of the No Hesitation podcast. Luka Doncic is averaging a stunning 38.6 ppg this season for the Western Conference leaders, putting himself in the MVP conversation. To point out just how prolific Doncic’s scoring streak is, podcast host Drew Hanlen pointed out that he is attempting almost as many shots this season as Sophie Cunningham did the entire WNBA season, and has already overtaken her for free-throws. He said: “Through his first nine games, he has attempted 221 shots. Last season in 43 games, you attempted 226 shots, so he is five behind you this season…. The second thing is, Luka has attempted 102 free throws already after nine games, and last season you attempted 74.” Sophie Cunningham asks for fairer comparison Sophie Cunningham pointed out that Luka Doncic makes a huge amount more money than she does. And instead, she asked to be compared to another Los Angeles Lakers players who she shares a more similar level of production with. She said: “And I also think you’re missing a big one: he also makes $50 million a year. I make $700,000 on my WNBA check. “You should compare me more to Quentin Grimes, we average around eight to 10 points, I think that’s it. My three-point shooting is actually better than the both of them. So if we’re going to compare, let’s compare.” It should be pointed out that Quentin Grimes is coming off the bench this season for the Lakers. His best season averaged was in 2024-25 where he posted 14.6ppg split across his spells with the Dallas Mavericks and Philadelphia 76ers. His 28-game spell exclusively with the Sixers saw him post 21.9 ppg. Sophie Cunningham’s best scoring WNBA regular season was in 2022 with the Phoenix Mercury, where she averaged 12.6 points per game. Grimes is making $13.9m with the Lakers this season as part of a four-year $60m deal signed in the offseason.
